pairs.evidence: crates/store-firestore/src/labels.rs:171 insert_calibration writes through put_doc, a PATCH upsert that rest.rs itself calls a silent overwrite on an insert path, and POST calibrations keeps a client-supplied id (crates/api/src/labels.rs:196), so re-posting an existing id rewrites a past judge-drift measurement where SQLite answers Conflict.

techniques.evidence: crates/store-firestore/src/labels.rs:171 Drift is read from the calibration history, and this write can replace a row in it; rest.rs offers create_doc with exists=false, which this path does not use.

crates/store-firestore/src/datasets.rs:94 No order key, and item ids are UUIDv4 document ids. Firestore's default order is by document name, so adding a case to an unfrozen dataset can land mid-list and shift later positions. The runner assigns case_index from this order and the regression diff joins runs on it, with no check of dataset version.
crates/store-firestore/src/collective.rs:120 The store returns collective rows unsorted and publishes no order; any ranking is made above this layer.

pairs.evidence: crates/store/src/sqlite/scores.rs:39 A verdict is tied to its scenario only by a 1-based position (the schema documents case_index that way, and scores has no dataset-item column), and the regression diff pairs runs on that position, so a changed case list compares different scenarios under one index.

techniques.evidence: crates/store/src/sqlite/datasets.rs:113 This query has no ORDER BY although the position derives from it and two indexes can serve it, the same plan-dependence benchmarks.rs documents for list_runs. Dataset version and frozen state exist, but the standard names positional identity as the failure and asks for a stable id on the scored case.

crates/store/src/sqlite/calibrations.rs:3 Judged only for this store's slice: append-only drift history, with a duplicate id refused as Conflict at line 47. Whether judge instructions are versioned belongs to the engine and runner and was not settled here.
crates/store/src/sqlite/score_summary.rs:71 Buckets return with n and a 95% interval and no ORDER BY; this layer publishes no order for the precondition to guard.
